title: Top K Frequent Elements
description: Return the k most frequent values using counting, bucket sort, or a bounded min-heap.

data.text: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the `k` most frequent elements in any order.
Every approach starts by counting occurrences in a dictionary. That is O(n) and unavoidable.

data.title: Frequency counting O(n)
data.content: One pass builds the count table.

data.text: Sort the distinct values by count and take the first `k`. O(m log m) where `m` is the number of distinct values.

data.title: Sort by count O(m log m)
data.content: Correct but sorts all distinct values.

data.text: A frequency can only be between 1 and n, so create n+1 buckets and place each value in the bucket matching its count. Then read buckets from the highest frequency downwards. This is O(n) and dominates any sorting approach.

data.title: Bucket sort O(n)
data.content: Frequency is a bounded integer, so it can be used as an array index.

data.text: Keep a min-heap of size k keyed on frequency. This is the right choice when the input is a *stream* and you cannot see all distinct values at once.

data.title: Min-heap of size k — O(m log k)
Bucket sort is the expected answer
data.text: When the problem claims a solution 'better than O(n log n)' exists, that is a hint that frequency bounds the keys and an array-indexed bucket sort is intended.

data.caption: Counts map into frequency-indexed buckets; reading from the top yields the most frequent values first.
data.definition:
graph TD
    A["nums = [1,1,1,2,2,3]"] --> B["counts: 1->3, 2->2, 3->1"]
    B --> C["buckets[1] = [3]"]
    C --> D["buckets[2] = [2]"]
    D --> E["buckets[3] = [1]"]
    E --> F["read f=3 -> 1, f=2 -> 2, stop at k=2"]
    F --> G["result [1,2]"]
    style G fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#2e7d32

cards.title: Sort by frequency
cons: O(m log m) even when k = 1

cards.title: Bucket sort
cons: O(n) buckets even when m is small

data.title: Complete solution
data.content: Choose based on constraints: buckets when all data is available and you want linear time, the heap when `k` is tiny or the data streams, sorting only for throwaway scripts.
